findings.reasoning: The finding claims a reentrancy issue in scaledEntropyCallback, but the ground truth target vulnerability is about setPayoutCalculator using the wrong calculator during settlement. The root cause is completely different - this is about external call reentrancy vs. state management of payout calculator. The location is also wrong (scaledEntropyCallback vs setPayoutCalculator).

The finding claims an access control issue with runJackpot being permissionless, but the ground truth target vulnerability is about setPayoutCalculator using the wrong calculator during settlement. The root cause is completely different - this is about who can call runJackpot vs. state management of payout calculator. The location is also wrong (runJackpot vs setPayoutCalculator).

The finding claims an integer overflow/underflow issue in _calculateTicketTierId, but the ground truth target vulnerability is about setPayoutCalculator using the wrong calculator during settlement. The root cause is completely different - this is about arithmetic operations vs. state management of payout calculator. The location is also wrong (_calculateTicketTierId vs setPayoutCalculator).

notes: None of the LLM's findings match the target vulnerability. The ground truth specifies a logic_error in setPayoutCalculator where swapping the calculator during settlement uses the new calculator's logic instead of the one active when tickets were purchased. All three findings are about completely different vulnerabilities in different functions. The LLM did not detect the target vulnerability at all.
